'''Raphaël Arlettaz''' (born 28 August 1961) is a Swiss conservation biologist, restoration ecologist, and professor at the [[University of Bern]]. He is known for his research on the ecology and conservation of threatened species, the restoration of degraded ecosystems, and his role in bridging academic research and applied biodiversity management in Switzerland and internationally.<ref name="one">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Raphaël Arlettaz |url=https://www.cb.iee.unibe.ch/about_us/prof_dr_arlettaz_raphal/index_eng.html |website=Conservation Biology |date=6 December 2023}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Arlettaz was born in [[Sion, Switzerland|Sion]], in the canton of [[Valais]], Switzerland, and grew up in the nearby village of Fully. He studied at the [[University of Fribourg]], earning a diploma's degree in natural sciences.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rencontre avec Raphaël Arlettaz, un spécialiste de la biodiversité {{!}} RTS |url=https://www.rts.ch/audio-podcast/2017/audio/rencontre-avec-raphael-arlettaz-un-specialiste-de-la-biodiversite-25519124.html |website=rts.ch |language=fr |date=1 December 2017}}</ref> He completed his doctoral studies in biology at the [[University of Lausanne]] in 1994, with a dissertation on the ecology of sibling mouse-eared bats ''Myotis myotis'' and ''Myotis blythii'', analysing their zoogeography, niche partitioning and foraging ecology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raphaël Arlettaz |url=https://scholar.google.ch/citations?user=6dGyCwoAAAAJ&hl=de |website=Google Scholar}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Following his doctoral work, Arlettaz held research and teaching positions at the Swiss Ornithological Institute and the University of Lausanne, and completed postdoctoral research supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation at the Universities of Lausanne, [[University of Aberdeen|Aberdeen]], [[University of Bristol|Bristol]] and [[University of Erlangen-Nuremberg|Erlangen-Nüremberg]]. In 2001 he was appointed full professor of Conservation Biology at the University of Bern, where he became head of the Division of Conservation Biology and co-director of the Institute of Ecology and Evolution. He also served as acting director of the institute from 2008 to 2010 and as acting director of the Department of Biology in 2019–2020.<ref name="chair">{{cite web |title=Raphaël Arlettaz, l'écologie en chaire et dans la chair - Le Temps |url=https://www.letemps.ch/sciences/environnement/raphael-arlettaz-lecologie-chaire-chair?srsltid=AfmBOoq8CwSM4lF_00u6SRbPFhykk5oR0OuoyhLXNVupnDG1Jk6vdIBI |website=letemps |language=fr |date=30 April 2019}}</ref>

In addition to his university work, Arlettaz founded and co-directed the Valais Field Station of the [[Swiss Ornithological Institute]] (2000–2012), which focuses on monitoring and applied conservation of endangered farmland, forest and Alpine birds. He was also the founder of the Valais Bat Network (1979), the Groupe Ornithologique Valaisan (1981), the Bearded Vulture Network Western Switzerland (1987) and Fauna.vs (1997), the Valais association of wildlife biologists, which he led for years. He is also the founder of the Valais Nature Foundation (2026).<ref name=":1" /> His dual engagement in academia and hands-on conservation has been noted for effectively linking research with on-the-ground biodiversity management.<ref>{{cite web |title=SNSF Data Portal |url=https://data.snf.ch/grants/person/66336 |website=data.snf.ch |language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
Arlettaz's research integrates [[population biology]], [[Behavioral ecology|behavioural ecology]], [[Community (ecology)|community ecology]], [[population dynamics]], [[Ecophysiology|eco-physiology]] and landscape management to address conservation problems across farmland, forest, river, and Alpine ecosystems.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |last1=Huber |first1=Martina |title=Biodiversität: Naturschutzbiologe Raphaël Arlettaz im Interview |url=https://www.nzz.ch/wissenschaft/wie-steht-es-um-die-biodiversitaet-herr-professor-zu-behaupten-die-situation-heute-sei-gut-ist-schlichtweg-falsch-ld.1844608 |website=Neue Zürcher Zeitung |language=de |date=3 September 2024}}</ref> Early in his career, he investigated the trophic ecology, acoustic behaviour and host-parasite relationships of European bats, publishing influential work on niche differentiation, foraging strategies, and eco-physiology.<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last1=Popa-Lisseanu |first1=Ana G. |last2=Delgado-Huertas |first2=Antonio |last3=Forero |first3=Manuela G. |last4=Rodríguez |first4=Alicia |last5=Arlettaz |first5=Raphaël |last6=Ibáñez |first6=Carlos |title=Bats' Conquest of a Formidable Foraging Niche: The Myriads of Nocturnally Migrating Songbirds |journal=PLOS ONE |pages=e205 |language=en |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0000205 |date=14 February 2007 |volume=2 |issue=2 |pmid=17299585 |pmc=1784064 |bibcode=2007PLoSO...2..205P |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Since joining the University of Bern, his group has carried out extensive comparative and experimental research on biodiversity-friendly management, particularly in agricultural landscapes such as grasslands, vineyards and fruit tree plantations. He demonstrated that conventional [[Agri-environmental measures|agri-environmental schemes]] in Europe often fail to sustain insectivorous vertebrates such as birds and bats because of insufficient prey availability, notably due to limited accessibility of foraging habitats following agricultural intensification.<ref name=":0" /> His real site-scale, full factorial and controlled grassland experiments showed that delaying mowing and maintaining uncut refuges can dramatically increase invertebrate abundance and benefit higher trophic levels, findings that have influenced Swiss and European agri-environmental policy and practice.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-04-21 |title=HUMAIN PASSIONNÉMENT reçoit Raphaël Arlettaz |url=https://canal9.ch/fr/humain-passionnement-recoit-raphael-arlettaz/ |access-date=2026-03-27 |website=Canal9 |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

Other projects have extended to the conservation of Alpine wildlife and the effects of land-use change, climate destruction and recreation (stress ecology) on mountain bird populations. Additional research areas include riverine restoration, forest biodiversity management, predator–prey relationships (apex carnivores and their ungulate prey), population dynamics of birds and bats, and the ecological impacts of renewable energy infrastructure, notably wind turbines, on bats and birds.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Arlettaz | first1=Raphaël | last2=Mathevet | first2=Raphaël |title=Raphaël Arlettaz | journal=Natures Sciences Sociétés |url=https://www.nss-journal.org/articles/nss/pdf/2010/04/nss10410.pdf | date=2010 | volume=18 | issue=4 | pages=452–458 | doi=10.1051/nss/2011009 }}</ref>

He is the author of more than 220 publications in international peer-reviewed journals, several dozens of chapters in collective books, more than 50 scientific notes and numerous outreach articles. His public engagement includes interviews in newspapers, radio and television in French, German, English and Spanish, as well as frequent lectures to scientific and general audiences.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raphaël Arlettaz |url=https://www.cb.iee.unibe.ch/e58880/e258374/e258539/CVRA_eng.pdf |website=cb.iee.unibe.ch}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Arlettaz has received numerous awards for his scientific contributions, including the Prof. Henri A. Guénin Prize (University of Lausanne, 1995) and the Prof. Schläfli Prize (Swiss Academy of Science, 1996) for his doctoral work, as well as the Research Medal of the [[Association for the Study of Animal Behaviour]] (1997) and the Elisabeth Rentschler Stiftung Prize for Animal Protection (2001). He has also been a laureate of the Swiss Youth Science (1982) and other prizes in Switzerland and abroad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Série Biodiversité, dernier volet avec l’interview de Raphaël Arlettaz, biologiste valaisan connu comme « Monsieur Biodiversité » |url=https://www.rts.ch/play/tv/19h30/video/serie-biodiversite-dernier-volet-avec-linterview-de-raphal-arlettaz-biologiste-valaisan-connu-comme--monsieur-biodiversite-?urn=urn:rts:video:9687138 |website=rts.ch}}</ref>

In 2015 he served as an author for the Europe and Central Asia assessment of the [[Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services]] (IPBES). He has been continuously funded by the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] since the mid-1990s, mostly for applied research projects.<ref name="chair" />
